newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria PM urges parliament to fight crime.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria PM urges parliament to fight crime.

text.p: Bulgarian Prime Minister Ivan Kostov appealed to parliament on Friday to amend laws in order to crack down on organised crime and corruption, which has run rampant since the collapse of communism.

"We cannot close our eyes to the fact that some members of the (state) security services have gone over the barrier and now play a key role in crime," Kostov told parliament, according to state radio.
Kostov suggested specific amendments to the criminal code mainly to combat violent behaviour, the domestic arms trade and the establishment of big organised criminal groups, the radio said.

He also stressed the need to combat economic crime by revamping laws related to fraud and embezzlement, tax evasion, unlawful insurance sales and misuse of official duties in the privatisation process.
Many former security service employees and sportsmen whose careers ended with the fall of communism now hire out their brawn to private security firms and insurance companies.
Parliament is expected to begin debate shortly on tightening anti-crime laws.

Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev said recently that the Bulgarian legal system had only a limited ability to fight organised crime and the ministry was hampered by out-of-date legislation but was drafting new laws to go before parliament.

Bulgaria's new government, which took over on May 21 after the Union of Democratic Forces won April general elections, has vowed to stem the crime and corruption which flourished in the seven years since the end of one-party rule.
Police said last week it would step up a campaign against corruption in their own ranks and against white-collar crime by recruiting experts in economics, law and computer technology.
Experts from the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation are in Bulgaria to give the police technical assistance in probing tax evasion and misappropriation of funds.
The Interior Ministry's first step was a high-profile check on luxury cars dubbed Operation Mosquito, to crack down on car theft and tax evasion in March.
Police began spot checks on the property of customs officers at border check-points aimed at cracking down on ill-gotten gains.
It also started checking firms operating in Bulgaria's Black Sea resorts.
